as_told.title: Navy stonewalls FOIA requests for Brown's records

plain: Michels says that when the daughter of the scientist Townsend Brown, Linda Brown, and Brown's biographer, Paul Schatzkin, asked the Navy for his records, the Navy was at first very uncooperative. In his documentary on Brown, whom he presents as having built UFO-like craft long before others, he adds that Schatzkin used the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and that the Navy at first acted as if it had never heard of a man by that name. Michels believes Brown's work is probably still classified by the Navy today, which, if true, would mean it was considered too sensitive to release.
